title: Drift Catalyst: Biweekly Regression Brief & Action Plan (2026-04-02)
content:
Executive summary:

This brief summarizes the biweekly regression telemetry for newly onboarded models and prompt-sets (period: 2026-03-19 — 2026-04-02). We observed a cluster of related quality regressions concentrated in conversational prompt cohorts for two recently onboarded model variants (v2-alpha, v2-beta-quant). Overall token-level accuracy proxies drop by 3.8% relative to baseline; customer-visible hallucination incidents rose from 0.9% to 2.6% in those cohorts. This doc catalogs the top failure archetypes, root hypotheses, short-term mitigations, and a prioritized action plan with clear owners and estimated delivery dates.

Key signals and what changed:
- Cohort-level drift: prompt-set cohorts labeled "support-chat", "billing-flow", and an internal eval subset "safety-stress" show largest delta. The distribution shift is concentrated in: shorter dialog turns (<= 20 tokens), high-latency KV cache eviction paths, and prompts with domain-specific entities (invoice numbers, product SKUs).
- Metric waterfalls (computed from nightly onboarding-eval runs):
  - Prompt-level pass rate (binary) aggregate: baseline 92.4% -> current 88.6% (-3.8pp)
  - Hallucination proxy (entity hallucination detector): 0.9% -> 2.6%
  - Safety trigger false-positive rate: 1.1% -> 1.7% (small but noticeable)
  - Latency tail (95th pct): +24ms on v2-beta-quant compared to v1-stable
- Coverage gaps: two prompt templates in the "billing-flow" set are missing expected slot-filling ground-truths in the onboarding harness (data issue introduced during last promptset merge).

Top 7 failure archetypes (ranked by incidence and user impact):
1) Token truncation on short-turn Qs
   - Symptom: model answers abruptly cut off mid-sentence for 8–12 token replies
   - Example prompt: "What's the tax code for invoice XYZ-243?" -> response ends with "The tax code is 12" and stops
   - Hypothesis: quantization pipeline + KV cache boundary causes early stop token misprediction in low-context turns
2) Entity hallucination in SKU lookup scenarios
   - Symptom: plausible-looking but incorrect SKUs returned when prompt implies lookup
   - Example prompt: "Find SKU for SuperWidget Pro serial AB-921" -> returns SKU AB-927 (nonexistent)
   - Hypothesis: model over-generalizes from token co-occurrence; prompt conditioning insufficient
3) Safety filter drift (overblocking)
   - Symptom: non-problematic but sensitive-looking customer queries flagged and truncated
   - Example: polite refund request flagged with unnecessary escalation language
   - Hypothesis: new model embeddings shifted safety classifier boundary; classifier not re-calibrated for quantized embeddings
4) Soft prompt mismatch with new temperature defaults
   - Symptom: response style deviates (too terse) causing downstream parsing failures
   - Hypothesis: default sampling param change during onboarding; prompt templates assume lower temperature
5) Referential context loss in multi-turn
   - Symptom: model loses earlier turn entity references after KV cache eviction on long sessions
   - Hypothesis: KV caching TTL default reduced; eviction not aligned with typical session lengths
6) Rerank regressions on short lists
   - Symptom: reranker picks lower-quality candidate for top-1 when list size <=3
   - Hypothesis: cached embeddings for reranker were not updated for v2-alpha; similarity metric drift
7) Numeric precision drop for currency/math outputs
   - Symptom: rounding errors on invoice totals, off-by-one cents
   - Hypothesis: quantized arithmetic path introduces bias in decimal formatting tokens

Immediate triage & mitigations (0–7 days):
- Rollback option: pin critical customer-facing routes to v1-stable for any live customer using the affected prompt-sets (owner: Noah Kim, ETA: 24h).
- Prompt-set patch: add guard tokens and explicit example-based constraints for invoice/SKU lookups (owner: Lena Ortiz, ETA: 48h).
- Quick re-calibration: run safety classifier recalibration using v2-alpha embeddings subset (owner: Aisha Patel, ETA: 72h).
- Hotfix in serving runtime: force KV cache TTL extension for sessions > 10 turns to avoid premature eviction (owner: SRE oncall / Rajiv, ETA: 48h).
- Canary rollback plan documented in console: add canary route with automatic fallback to v1-stable if hallucination proxy > 2% for 1h (owner: Marco Chen, ETA: 24h).

Medium-term investigations (7–30 days):
- Re-run onboarding-eval with controlled quantization ablations: baseline, q4, q8, q8hf to isolate precision-vs-quality curves (owner: eng-applied-ml experiment owners, ticket: ML-1423, ETA: 14 days).
- Prompt augmentation: expand promptset coverage with edge cases from production customer transcripts (owner: solutions-eng, ETA: 10 days).
- Reranker retraining with fresh embeddings and calibration on small-list tasks (owner: applied-ml reranker team, ETA: 21 days).
- Latency profiling: microbench the v2-beta-quant token-gen path to identify kernel-level sources of 95th pct latency spike (owner: serving-runtime perf, ETA: 14 days).

Action item tracker (prioritized):
- [P0] Pin routes: Noah Kim -> implement pins + monitor (24h)
- [P0] Canary fallback: Marco Chen -> ensure automated fallback + slack alert (24h)
- [P1] Safety recalibration: Aisha Patel -> run new calibration + retest (72h)
- [P1] Fix promptset coverage gaps: Lena Ortiz -> patch two billing-flow templates (48h)
- [P2] Onboarding ablation runs: applied-ml -> schedule controlled experiments (14d)
- [P2] Reranker refresh: reranker lead -> retrain with updated embeddings (21d)
- [P3] KV TTL production tweak: SRE -> apply TTL extension and monitor evictions (48h)

Monitoring & dashboards (what to watch):
- New panels to add to the biweekly regression dashboard:
  - Hallucination proxy by prompt cohort (7d moving avg) [alert threshold: 1.5%->page]
  - Prompt-level pass-rate heatmap (rows: prompt-template, cols: model-variant)
  - KV-eviction count correlated with abrupt-stop incidents (scatter plot)
  - Safety filter false-positive rate by model and by embedding-quant config
- Nightly onboarding-eval changes: add a small, fast smoke-check that runs the 30 highest-impact prompts in each cohort and surfaces deltas via daily slack digest (owner: Marco Chen).

Hypotheses to validate (ranked):
- H1 (High confidence): Quantization path interacts with low-context turn generation causing early-stop tokens -> validate with q-ablation experiments.
- H2 (Medium): Safety classifier drift due to embedding distribution shift -> validate by recalibrating and measuring FP/FN deltas.
- H3 (Medium): Prompt template regression from recent merges removed slot ground-truths -> validate by comparing prompt manifest versions and re-running harness per-commit.
- H4 (Low): Serving kernel scheduling affected 95th pct latency for v2-beta-quant -> validate with perf traces and kernel selection logs.

Meeting cadence & owners:
- Triage sync (ad-hoc) — daily 09:30 (15m) until P0s closed — owners: Noah, Marco, Lena
- Deep dive (7-day) — 60m — review ablation results and reranker candidate refresh — owners: applied-ml, serving-runtime
- Stakeholder update (biweekly) — 30m — product + solutions-eng summary of impact and mitigation status

Notes / dirty list (things surfaced in triage but not prioritized yet):
- Some prompt variants in the internal "safety-stress" cohort appear to be duplicates with slightly different paraphrases; consolidation could reduce noise in signal.
- A small subset of onboarding harness runs failed due to a flaky data ingestion job on 2026-03-25; those logs live in ML-agnostic S3 path: s3://redwood-onboard-logs/2026-03-25 (owner: infra).

Appendix: sample failure artifacts (sanitized)
- Prompt: "How do I change billing address for account 12345?"
  Expected: stepwise instructions with account link
  Actual (v2-beta-quant): "To change billing address, go to your profile -> Security -> then..." (incorrect nav path)
- Prompt: "Return invoice total for INV-44321"
  Expected: precise currency amount 147.20 USD
  Actual: 147.2 USD -> parsed downstream as 147.20? (parsing mismatch)

If anything in here should be escalated to enterprise customers immediately (eg. P0 incidents hitting production SLAs), call out on #prod-alerts and tag @oncall-sre.

Next steps (today):
1) Noah to pin critical routes and confirm via dashboard that customer-visible hallucinations drop to baseline (24h).
2) Marco to create canary fallback route and add the nightly smoke-check to the onboarding-eval runner (24h).
3) Lena to patch the two missing billing-flow prompt templates and push new prompt manifest (48h).

Prepared by: Marco Chen (applied-ml)
